title: The Rights Revolution Spreads
objective: After this level you can explain how women, farmworkers and Native activists built on the civil rights movement, from Title IX to tribal self-government, and why the ERA stalled.
summary: Title IX (1972), farmworkers’ grape contracts (1970) and tribal self-determination (1975) built on civil rights. The ERA passed Congress but fell three states short.

cards.headline: The civil rights movement wrote a playbook. Others picked it up.
cards.body: What did women, farmworkers and Native nations win, and why did one amendment fall short?

cards.headline: Title IX
cards.body: Title IX (1972) says no person shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from any education program receiving federal money. President Richard Nixon signed it on June 23, 1972. One sentence, and every school taking federal dollars had to open its doors to girls and women.

cards.headline: Grapes and a boycott
cards.body: In September 1965, Filipino American grape workers led by Larry Itliong went on strike in Delano, California. Itliong persuaded César Chávez and Dolores Huerta’s mostly Mexican American union to join, and in 1966 the unions merged into what became the United Farm Workers. After a national grape boycott, growers signed contracts in 1970 promising better pay and benefits.

cards.headline: Self-determination
cards.body: In November 1969, activists calling themselves Indians of All Tribes occupied Alcatraz Island, claiming it as Indian land, and held it for 19 months. In 1970 President Nixon called for “self-determination without termination.” The Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act of 1975 let tribal governments run their own federal programs.

cards.headline: The ERA stalls
cards.body: Alice Paul wrote the Equal Rights Amendment, first introduced in 1923. It passed Congress in 1972, and 35 of the 38 states needed ratified it. Supporters said it would guarantee that rights could not be denied “on account of sex.” Phyllis Schlafly’s STOP ERA (“Stop Taking Our Privileges”) argued it would take away protections women already had. The deadline, extended to 1982, passed three states short.

cards.headline: The rights revolution: explained
learned: Title IX (1972) barred sex discrimination in schools
Tribes won the right to run federal programs (1975)
The ERA fell three states short of ratification

questions.prompt: Which rights victory of this era came from a 1975 law on Native nations?

options.label: Schools had to stop excluding students by sex
Grape growers signed contracts with farmworkers
options.rationale: That was the farmworkers’ win, in 1970.

options.label: Tribal governments could run their own federal programs
Alcatraz Island was handed to Indians of All Tribes
options.rationale: The level says activists occupied it for 19 months, not that it was handed over.

questions.explanation: The Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act of 1975 let tribal governments run their own federal programs.

questions.prompt: Supporters and Phyllis Schlafly disagreed about the ERA. What was the core of their disagreement?

options.label: Whether women should be allowed to vote
options.rationale: Women had won the vote in 1920.

options.label: Whether Congress could pass amendments at all
Whether it guaranteed equality or took away women’s protections
Whether Alice Paul had really written it
options.rationale: Nobody in the level disputes that.

questions.explanation: Supporters said it guaranteed equal rights regardless of sex; Schlafly argued it would take away protections women already had.

questions.prompt: Level 69’s Alice Paul led the Silent Sentinels for the vote. What did she do next, as this level tells it?

options.label: She wrote the Equal Rights Amendment
She founded the United Farm Workers
options.rationale: Itliong, Chávez and Huerta’s unions merged into what became the UFW.

options.label: She signed Title IX into law
She led the Alcatraz occupation
options.rationale: Indians of All Tribes occupied Alcatraz.

questions.explanation: After the 19th Amendment, Alice Paul wrote the ERA, first introduced in 1923.
